'We can see that the Lord' is Mormon's own editorial idiom throughout this chapter ('and thus we see', 12:3), the psalm's imperative is a call to trust while Helaman 12:1's indicative is a complaint that trust does not last, and “put their trust in him” occurs in exactly three KJV verses, none of them Psalm 34.

The senses are opposed and instructively so. Helaman 12:18-19's treasure is hidden, cursed, and never recovered by anyone. The episode behind it is Achan's, where “hid in the earth” occurs in exactly one KJV verse, Joshua 7:21, and where the buried valuables bring a curse on the man who buried them. A five-word match worth writing up, because a careless reader could take it and because the two sentences are about entirely different things. 1 Corinthians 7:7 is Paul on celibacy — 'For I would that all men were even as I myself' — a wish about marital state, immediately qualified by 'but every man hath his proper gift of God'. Helaman 12:25 is Mormon on universal salvation: 'And I would that all men might be saved. But we read that in that great and last day, there are some which shall be cast out.' The optative construction is identical and the content shares nothing. What the verse does borrow is at its end: 'cast off from the presence of the Lord' is the KJV's judgment idiom of 2 Thessalonians 1:9, recorded as a composite at the 12:26 link.
